headline: China's CXMT hits 12nm-class DRAM milestone with 5th-gen tech, boosting die capacity by 50%
summary: The new G5 process reduces active-area half-pitch to 11.95nm and enables 24Gb LPDDR5X devices with 50% more capacity. These chips are already in mass production for Chinese flagship smartphones.
details: China's DRAM champion CXMT has begun mass production using its 5th-generation DRAM process technology, G5. The first devices are 24Gb LPDDR5X, offering 50% more capacity than previous comparable products and are already in mainstream Chinese flagship smartphones.

The G5 process reduces DRAM
’s active-area half-pitch to 11.95nm using quadruple-patterning lithography. This puts it in the range of other advanced 10nm-class DRAM technologies, though it's not a direct node designation.

CXMT also modified its process flow and introduced new materials for storage capacitors with a depth-to-width aspect ratio of about 45:1. This high aspect ratio enables reduced DRAM cell area and more memory arrays per wafer.

While a significant achievement, CXMT's 11.95nm figure is an active-area half-pitch, not a conventional process node. Direct comparison with Micron, Samsung, and SK hynix is challenging without data on density, yields, and power consumption.
